subject: biology
title: Inherited disorders
key_idea: Some disorders are inherited through certain alleles. **Polydactyly** is caused by a dominant allele and **cystic fibrosis** by a recessive allele. **Embryo screening** can test for these alleles, but it raises economic, social and ethical issues.

blocks.text: Inherited disorders are caused by the alleles a person inherits. This section covers the two you must know.

items.meaning: A disorder caused by inheriting certain alleles from the parents.
Having extra fingers or toes. It is caused by a dominant allele.
A disorder of cell membranes. It is caused by a recessive allele.
A heterozygous person who has one recessive allele but does not have the disorder.

rows: Too much mucus in the lungs and digestive system

items: Mucus blocks the duct from the pancreas to the small intestine.
Fewer digestive enzymes enter the small intestine, so less food is digested.
Less glucose and fewer amino acids are absorbed into the blood.
So less glucose is available for respiration, and less protein is made for growth.
Mucus also blocks the tubes to the alveoli, so less oxygen enters the blood.
Less oxygen reaches the cells, so less energy is released by aerobic respiration.
Polydactyly: dominant allele. One copy is enough to have it.
Cystic fibrosis: recessive allele. Two copies are needed.
CF slows growth because less food is digested and less oxygen reaches the cells.

blocks.text: Use a genetic cross to predict the disorder. Choose the parents below and look at the children.

diagram.alt: Choose the genotypes of two parents to see the chance of their children having polydactyly, which is caused by a dominant allele.

items: A person with polydactyly may have the genotype Dd. They have the disorder because the dominant allele is expressed.
Two parents who are both Hh carriers of cystic fibrosis have a 25% chance of a child with CF. The cross is in the notes on genetic crosses.
Two parents with no CF who have a child with CF must both be carriers.
One allele in every 50 in the UK population is the CF allele. A person needs two, so about 1 person in 2500 has CF (1/50 × 1/50).

blocks.text: When neither parent has the allele

items: Two parents may have no alleles for polydactyly, and still have a child with it.
This is caused by a **mutation**, a change in the base sequence, in the formation of a gamete (during meiosis).
The mutation changes the amino acid sequence, so a different protein is made (or none).
The child who has the mutated allele has the disorder, because the allele is dominant.
One dominant allele is enough for polydactyly.
CF needs two recessive alleles, so both parents of an affected child are carriers.
A new mutation in a gamete can cause a disorder in a family with no history of it.

blocks.text: Embryo screening tests an embryo's DNA to find out its genotype. This section covers the methods and the issues.

items: Screening finds out whether an embryo has the alleles for an inherited disorder such as CF.
In one method, a fine needle takes a sample of the fluid around the embryo after about 10 weeks of pregnancy, and the DNA is tested. The test has a small risk of miscarriage.
In another method, a couple use in vitro fertilisation (IVF) to make a small number of embryos. Each is tested, and only embryos without the disorder are implanted.
IVF is a stressful, invasive procedure. It often does not result in a baby, and the free public health service may not provide it to everyone who wants it.
Parents can find out if the embryo has an inherited disorder.
They can prepare for the baby, for example with early treatment.
They can decide whether to continue with the pregnancy.
Over time there are fewer people with inherited disorders.
There is a risk to the embryo or to the mother, such as miscarriage.
The process is stressful.
It may lead to termination of the pregnancy, or destruction of embryos.
The screening process may be costly.
The embryo cannot give consent.
It may increase prejudice against people who have inherited disorders.

blocks.text: Embryo screening and gene therapy may reduce suffering. They also raise ethical issues, so you may be asked for an informed judgement from the information given.

items: Embryo screening tests an embryo's genotype for alleles that cause disorders.
Give specific advantages and specific arguments against.
Use the information in the question to support a judgement.

checks.q: Polydactyly is caused by a dominant allele, D. A person has the genotype Dd. Do they have polydactyly? Explain.
checks.a: Yes. The dominant allele is expressed even if only one copy is present.

checks.q: Give two advantages of embryo screening.
checks.a: Any two from: can find out if the embryo has an inherited disorder; can prepare for the baby; can decide whether to continue with the pregnancy; fewer people with inherited disorders over time.

checks.q: Give two arguments against embryo screening. Do not refer to religion.
checks.a: Any two from: risk to the embryo; risk to the mother (miscarriage); stressful process; may lead to termination of the pregnancy; cost; the embryo cannot give consent.

worked_example.question:
In a person with CF, cells lining the lungs and digestive system create too much mucus.

The mucus can:
- block the duct leading from the pancreas to the small intestine
- block the tubes leading to the alveoli in the lungs.

Explain why children with CF grow more slowly than children without CF.
answer_points: Fewer (digestive) enzymes enter the small intestine, so the enzymes break down less food.
So there is less absorption of nutrients: less glucose enters the blood, so less glucose is available for respiration.
Fewer amino acids enter the blood, so less protein is made for growth.
Less oxygen enters the blood and reaches the cells, so less oxygen is available for aerobic respiration.
So less energy is released for growth.
worked_example.tip: Marked in levels. For Level 3 (5 to 6 marks) you must link the points logically and include both the enzymes and the oxygen.
